name: Rolled, stabilised with a hydraulic binder (stabilise)
process: As rolled.self-binding, but the sand is premixed with a small share of hydraulic binder (lime or cement) before it is laid, wetted and rolled, so that it sets into a weak, still-porous crust: the French 'sable stabilise'. It keeps the sand's colour and look and bears more traffic; under heavy loads it still breaks down to dust.
processSources: Bronzo Perasso (Marseille), 'Sable naturel pour sols stabilises 0/6,3' (concasse, petrographie calcaire, for sols stabilises) and the linked product 'Sable traite pour sols stabilises (3,5%, 5%, 7%)', read 2026-09-26, https://bronzoperasso.fr/produit/sable-naturel-pour-sols-stabilises-0-63/
Koncrete, 'Sable 0/6 livre en vrac', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.koncrete.fr/produits/sable-0-6

binder.note: The share's basis (by mass of dry sand) is not stated on the product listing.

look.text: A mixture of sand and cement that forms a compact, lasting stabilised surface and 'conserve la couleur naturelle du sable et son aspect rustique'.
look.source: Colas & Vous, 'Sable stabilise', product page read 2026-09-26, https://www.colasetvous.fr/produits/sable-stabilise/

failure.text: Under trucks and heavy crowds it breaks into a fine grey powder; the Tuileries sought 15 million euros to replace it.
failure.source: franceinfo, 'Les jardins des Tuileries recherchent 15 millions pour eradiquer la poussiere' (3 May 2013), https://www.franceinfo.fr/culture/patrimoine/les-jardins-des-tuileries-recherchent-15-millions-pour-eradiquer-la-poussiere_3310669.html

photograph: Like the self-binding walk but firmer and with less loose grit; edges crumble where it is thin.

unverified.reason: Whether the listed 3.5-7 % is by mass of sand or of the mix was not stated.
